nws.synopsis: Lingering scattered showers will bring light rain to areas west of the mountains today, becoming more confined to San Diego County this evening. Weak offshore flow expected Saturday and Sunday. Dry and warmer for the weekend through Monday, then gradually cooler for the middle of next week with a chance of precipitation for late next week. Tides will increase over the weekend, remaining elevated through much of next week.
systems: By tonight, models are showing a closed upper level low moving south and east towards the border of California and Arizona.
This will turn the pressure gradient weakly offshore, increasing north to northeasterly winds in wind prone locations.
Given the unsettled weather quickly turning to offshore flow, marine layer low clouds and fog will largely be absent from the coast into early next week.
nws.aviation: 240015Z...SHRA are moving though the high desert and IE this evening, slowly pushing south across the region (west of mtns), then sweeping through San Diego county through ~06z. VCSH for coastal southern SD County through 10z. Bases generally 4-9 kft through the evening; SHRA to bring briefly MVFR (locally IFR) vis/cigs. As SHRA departs, BKN/OVC clouds scatter out in the lowlands from north to south this evening through tonight. Mostly VFR and clear by sunrise Sat with N/NE winds (gusting up to 30 kts) developing overnight through the morning around (and south of) the Cajon Pass and along coast facing slopes.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing: offshore mornings put launch in the lee. Glass-off common late in the day.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; strong midday air in summer.

sites.name: Elsinore (E / Edwards)
sites.note: East-facing over the lake. A strong west wind over the ridge means rotor; the sea-breeze convergence line is the XC engine. Evening glass-off over the lake.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Mostly a wind site: steady W to WNW sea breeze. On rare thermal days you get well above the cliffs (1,200 ft+); the radar flags those as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse
sites.note: Needs a real sea-breeze convergence: onshore SW at launch and no north or east wind aloft. Watch desert-slope wind advisories.

sites.name: Otay
sites.note: Near the border; XC only north and east.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Commercial flight park on the San Jacinto front.
